content: Secnidazole is indicated for the treatment of bacterial vaginosis in females. The recommended dosage is one packet (2 grams) of granules taken orally as a single dose, regardless of meal timing. For the treatment of trichomoniasis caused by Trichomonas vaginalis, it is essential to treat both the infected patient and their sexual partners simultaneously to prevent reinfection. The dosage is the same: one packet (2 grams) of granules taken orally as a single dose, without regard to meal timing. This regimen is not established for individuals under 12 years of age. For those aged 12 years and older, the same single-dose regimen applies. Alcohol consumption during secnidazole therapy and for at least two days after completing treatment should be avoided, as ethanol increases the toxicity of secnidazole. Adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dizziness, and headache have been reported when secnidazole is co-administered with alcohol. Patients should be advised to avoid alcoholic beverages and preparations containing ethanol or propylene glycol during and shortly after treatment. Reported adverse reactions include nausea, dysgeusia (altered taste), abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, and vomiting. Severe and irreversible hepatotoxicity, including acute liver failure with fatal outcomes, has been reported in patients with Cockayne syndrome. Secnidazole is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to secnidazole, its excipients, or other nitroimidazole derivatives. Vulvovaginal candidiasis may occur as a side effect of secnidazole treatment. Symptomatic cases may require antifungal therapy. Long-term use of secnidazole should be avoided due to carcinogenicity observed in mice and rats treated chronically with nitroimidazole derivatives, which are structurally related to secnidazole. Prescribing secnidazole in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection or prophylactic indication is not recommended, as it increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. Data on the use of secnidazole in pregnant women are insufficient to determine the risk of adverse developmental outcomes. However, animal reproduction studies in rats and rabbits have shown no adverse developmental effects when secnidazole was administered orally during organogenesis at doses up to four times the clinical dose. There is no information on the presence of secnidazole in human milk, its effects on the breastfed child, or its impact on milk production. Other nitroimidazole derivatives are known to be present in human milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, including tumorigenicity, breastfeeding is not recommended during secnidazole treatment and for 96 hours after administration. Secnidazole should be taken by sprinkling the entire contents of the packet onto applesauce, yogurt, or pudding. The mixture should be consumed within 30 minutes without chewing or crushing the granules. A glass of water should be consumed afterward to aid in swallowing. The secnidazole mixture is not intended to be dissolved in any liquid. Patients should take the entire packet at one time and should not save a portion of the medicine for later use. Secnidazole can be taken without regard to meal timing. Store secnidazole at room temperature, between 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted to 15–30°C (59–86°F).
